reason.auto: Best codec for this device and browser, picked at Connect
reason.autoChroma: Sharper takes full colour detail when both ends can do it
reason.chroma420: Colour at quarter resolution — the video default, decodes everywhere
reason.av1: Best quality per bit — hardware on both ends
reason.agentNoAv1: This device has no AV1 hardware encoder
reason.av1NoHw444: No hardware encoder can produce AV1 in 4:4:4
reason.hevc: Hardware H.265 on the device (NVENC / QSV / AMF / VideoToolbox / VAAPI / D3D12 / Vulkan)
reason.hevc444: Sharpest text on the hardware pipeline, ~1.5× bitrate
reason.browserNoHevc: This browser lacks a hardware HEVC decoder
reason.browserNoHevcRext: This browser can’t decode HEVC 4:4:4 (Chrome ≥137 with NVIDIA driver ≥572.16, or Intel Gen11+)
reason.agentNoHevc: This device has no HEVC encoder
reason.agentNoHevc444: This device has no HEVC 4:4:4 encoder (NVENC only today)
reason.browserNoVp9: This browser can’t decode VP9 profile 1
reason.agentNoVp9: This device has no VP9 encoder
reason.h264444: Sharpest text via H.264 High 4:4:4 — hardware encode, software decode
reason.browserNoH264High444: This browser can’t decode H.264 High 4:4:4
reason.agentNoH264_444: This device has no H.264 4:4:4 encoder (NVENC only today)
reason.vp9444hw: Sharpest text, ~1.5× bitrate — hardware encode (Intel), software decode
reason.failedBefore: Failed to decode on this browser earlier — retried after a browser or driver update
reason.no444Anywhere: No 4:4:4 cell exists for this device and browser

endedByHost.title: The person at the device ended the session.
endedByHost.body: They ended it from their screen (Disconnect, or their desktop's own Stop for screen sharing), so this viewer stays disconnected. Reconnect asks them again, as any new session does.

auth.heardAbout: How did you hear about Roomler?
auth.heardAboutHint: Optional. It tells us which channels work.

room.name: Room Name
room.noMessages: No messages yet. Start the conversation!

approval.notAccepted: The vault's policies do not accept your approval of this use

hive.title: Agent sessions
hive.adoptedExplain: A session you run in a terminal, mirrored here for you alone. It is read-only: nobody prompts it from Roomler.

empty.title: No agent sessions yet
empty.body: Start one on a device whose owner has turned agent sessions on (hive_enabled). It runs there, as the account the device maps you to, and its transcript stays on the device.

start.title: Start an agent session
start.folderHint: It must be inside one of the device's hive_roots.

viewer.truncated: The output was cut to the device's limit; its start and end are kept.
viewer.checkpoint: Checkpoint {n}: {changed} of {files} of the agent's files changed
viewer.unknownKind: An event this version cannot show ({kind}).

tool.tooLong: Too long to compare line by line.

viewer.askFailed: The prompt did not reach the agent.
viewer.readOnly: You can read this session and talk in its room. Only its drivers can prompt the agent.
viewer.adoptedReadOnly: This session runs in a terminal on its device, so it is read-only here: nobody prompts it from Roomler.
viewer.copyReadOnly: You are reading a copy another device holds, because the device that runs this session cannot serve it now. It is read-only: only that device takes prompts.
viewer.drivingRefused: You drive this session, but its device does not let you act there: {why}

approval.denyPlaceholder: Why not? (optional — the agent reads it)
approval.waiting: Waiting for one of the session's drivers to answer.
approval.expired: Nobody answered in time, so it did not run.
approval.failed: The answer did not reach the device.

people.title: Who takes part
people.explain: Drivers prompt the agent and answer its approvals. Readers read the session and talk in its room — nothing they write reaches the agent. Only the session's owner changes who takes part.
people.remove: Take them out of the session
people.adoptedReadersOnly: It runs in a terminal, so it takes readers only.

roomCopies.title: Copies of this session
roomCopies.explain: Each device listed holds a copy of this session, its transcript and checkpoints, so it stays readable, and can move, while the device it runs on is offline.

short.adopted: A session adopted from a terminal is copied nowhere but the device it runs on.
short.restricted: Fewer copies than the policy asks: a device that would hold one lacks a tag this session is restricted to.
short.no_device: Fewer copies than the policy asks: no other device offers to hold one.

step.joining: the device is taking its copy
step.draining: the device it runs on is finishing its turn

roomCopies.moveExplain: It stops where it runs and goes on there, from the copy that device holds. The copy that holds the most is picked: a move to one that holds less is refused.
roomCopies.folderHint: Where it runs on that device: the same folder unless you say otherwise.
roomCopies.ahead: {device} holds more of this session than any device it can move to: a move is refused until one catches up.
roomCopies.noTarget: No other device that runs sessions holds a copy yet.
roomCopies.adoptedStays: A session adopted from a terminal stays where it runs.

outcome.promoting: Moving: the device is ready, and the one it runs on is finishing its turn.
outcome.teleporting: Moving: the device is taking its copy while the session still runs.
outcome.pending: Asked: the device has not answered yet. Its room says how it goes on.

roomCopies.teleportExplain: Moves it to a device that holds no copy: that device takes one while the session still runs, then it moves there as a move to a copy does. The device it runs on must be online.
roomCopies.noTeleport: No other online device that runs sessions can take it.
roomCopies.forkExplain: Makes a new session from this one's conversation, in a folder of its own. This session goes on as it is.
roomCopies.forkFolderHint: Its own folder on that device: a fork cannot share the folder the session runs in.
roomCopies.noFork: No online device that runs sessions can make a fork.
roomCopies.adoptedNoFork: A session adopted from a terminal is not forked.
roomCopies.forkWhileMoving: It is being moved: fork it once it settles.

forkOutcome.accepted: Forked: the new session starts on that device.
forkOutcome.pending: Asked: the device has not answered yet. The fork's room says how it goes on.
forkOutcome.joining: Forking: the device is taking a copy first.

purge.title: Delete this session for good
purge.explain: "{title}" is deleted from every device that held it: where it runs, each copy, and where it ran before. On each, the account's part goes too, its history and its checkpoints, never the folder it worked in.
purge.atOnce: Its room, its core memory snapshot and its approvals are deleted at once. This cannot be undone.
purge.forksKeep: A session forked from it keeps its conversation up to its fork.
purge.going: Purging: {done} of {total} devices have answered. One offline is purged when it next connects.
purge.done: Purged from every device that held it.
purge.forks: Sessions forked from it keep its conversation up to their fork: {n}.
purge.pendingDetail: It is purged when it next connects.

closed.device_removed: The device was removed, and purged everything it held

manage.title: Make it a managed session
manage.explain: Its terminal session ended. Roomler can carry it on as a managed session on {device}: the same conversation, resumed from its terminal's own history, then run, copied and driven like any session started here.
manage.folderHint: Where its terminal ran, unless you name another
manage.lastRefused: Its device refused the last asking: {why}
manage.accepted: It is a managed session now, on {device}.
manage.pending: Asked. Its device has not answered yet: this room shows how it goes.

memory.title: Agent memory
memory.about: Facts kept here reach agent sessions as standing instructions. A session gets a copy when it starts and keeps that copy: a fact added later reaches the next session, not a running one. Only devices whose owner turned on hive_core_memory pass them to the agent.

scopeHint.org: Every session in the organization. Its administrators keep these.
scopeHint.device: Only sessions on that device. Device managers keep these.

memory.newFact: A fact the agent should know
memory.archive: Archive — out of every future session's memory

copies.title: Agent copies
copies.about: Each agent session runs on one device and is copied to the devices your organization's policy places it on, so it stays readable, and can move, while that device is offline. A copy is plaintext on the device that holds it.
copies.off: Sessions are not copied on this server: an operator turns on hive.replicaset.

policy.title: The policy
policy.copies: {min} to {max} copies of each session, its own device's among them
policy.archive: Archive replicas join every session the rules allow
policy.prefer: Then the session owner's own devices
policy.restricted: A session on a device tagged {tags} is copied only to devices with that tag
policy.retention: Kept {days} days after a session ends
policy.retentionForever: Kept for good after a session ends

rules.copiesHint: Copies of each session, its own device's among them: 1 to {max}
rules.maxBelowMin: At most is fewer than at least
rules.archive: Archive replicas join every session the rules allow
rules.prefer: Then the session owner's own devices
rules.restrictedHint: A session on a device with one of these tags is copied only to devices with that tag too. Press Enter to add one.
rules.retention: Days kept after a session ends
rules.retentionHint: 0 keeps it for good, and at most {max}
rules.retentionInvalid: A whole number of days, from 0 to {max}
rules.saved: Saved. The organization's live sessions are placed again under it.
rules.stale: The policy changed since you read it. It is shown as it is now: make your change again.

archive.title: Archive replicas
archive.hint: An always-on device of your organization that keeps a copy of every session the rules allow, for their retention, and serves a session while no other member is online. It runs no session. Your organization runs it, on its own machines.
archive.none: No device offers itself as an archive replica yet.
archive.unreadable: Until an archive replica is online, a session is readable only while one of its members is.
archive.offers: Offers itself as an archive replica
archive.notOffering: Does not offer itself: its owner turned hive_archive off, or it has not connected since
archive.gone: No longer a device of this organization
archive.stale: The policy changed since it was read. It is shown again: try once more.

add.title: Add an archive replica
add.intro: Run the archive replica image on a machine of your organization's that stays on. Its first start enrolls it with a token from here; every later start runs from its volume, and needs no token.
add.volume: The volume is the device: it holds the device's credentials and every session copied to it, in plaintext. Keep it as you would the sessions themselves.
add.hostname: Give the container a fixed hostname: the device's identity depends on it, and two archive replicas must not share one.
add.token: The token works once, for {minutes} minutes, and only the first start needs it.
add.next: Once it runs it appears under Archive replicas: turn on Designated to make it one.

search.label: Search the agent sessions you can read
search.hint: Searched on your organization's archive replica: what you type, and what it finds, never reach the server.
search.noRoom: That session has no room to open.

refused.not_found: Agent sessions cannot be searched in this organization.
refused.no_archive_replica: No archive replica that searches is online right now.
refused.no_session: The archive replica holds none of the sessions you can read yet.
refused.rate_limited: Too many searches were opened in the last minute. Wait a moment, then type again.
refused.too_many_views: This tab holds as many agent session peers as it may. Type again in a moment.
refused.device_unsupported: The archive replica runs a build that cannot search.
refused.no_answer: The archive replica did not answer.
refused.unavailable: The server could not prepare the search. Type again in a moment.
refused.at_capacity: The archive replica serves as many searches as it can right now.
refused.hive_disabled: The archive replica does not serve searches.

defaultPattern.label: Default pattern
defaultPattern.hint: What a viewer's Keep busy menu pre-selects on a device they have not set it on before. Circle unless you change it; a person's own last choice for a device wins over it.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Every time keep busy was turned on or off on a device, as the device reported it, and every change to these settings. Kept permanently.

sourceHint.device: What the device itself reported on a heartbeat: a claim, seen at the 30-second heartbeat, never a server decision.
sourceHint.server: The server's own record of an admin's change.

approval.title: Account approvals
approval.intro: Central account admission. Organization roles, device enrollment and operating-system permissions are separate.
approval.notEnabled: Account approval is not enabled on this server.
approval.ownerOnly: Only the central approval owner can access this console.
approval.revisionNote: The server must accept revision {revision} before any status changes.
approval.revokeWarning: This revokes account admission. Existing network and device sessions have their own revocation rules.

mine.title: My devices & sharing
mine.intro: Only devices owned by this account, across your active organizations. Organization-wide visibility is not ownership.
mine.ownedHint: Owned devices in active, joined organizations.
mine.distinctHint: Distinct devices with unrevoked, unexpired shares.
mine.countNote: A device shared more than once is counted once per direction. Retained records include expired and revoked shares. These are sharing-record states, not proof that a device is online or its service policy permits a connection.
mine.noneOwned: No devices owned by this account in active, joined organizations.
mine.nonePage: No devices on this page. Refresh or choose another page.
mine.footer: Device IDs and sharing records remain separate from connection state. Desktop access still requires the device's current service policy and consent.
mine.refreshFailed: Could not refresh personal device and sharing records. Previous records, if shown, may be stale. The server may need an update.

shares.title: Device shares
shares.intro: An explicit share grants one approved person access to one device. It does not add organization membership, LAN access, exit routing or resharing.
shares.listNote: {total} retained sharing records in this direction, not a unique-device count. Expired and revoked records remain visible. Each record identifies the device, grantor/recipient, permissions, creation, expiry, revocation and revision. Record state does not override device policy or consent.
shares.noOwned: No devices owned by this account
shares.recipientHint: The person must have an approved, verified account.
shares.formNote: Device consent and service settings still apply. Read-only file transfer is not supported by the current native file protocol. SSH sharing does not enable the device’s SSH service or organization policy. The approved recipient signs in through the native client with a hidden password prompt; a manually provisioned token file is optional. It does not enable desktop access or TCP forwarding.
shares.invalid: Choose a device, name the recipient by username or email, pick a supported capability, and an expiry of 1–720 hours.

ssh.title: SSH through the native client
ssh.intro: This is an access check and instructions, not an SSH session or a browser terminal. Device consent and SSH policy still apply. The device runs its built-in SSH server; it does not need a system sshd.
ssh.hostKey: Public host key (the native client verifies this identity):
ssh.run: Run the native CLI locally, replacing the server URL and account-name placeholders:
ssh.warning: The CLI still needs a local SSH client. With --login, enter your MeshHarbor account password at its hidden terminal prompt; the token remains in process memory. This page does not export your HttpOnly web session or launch a command. Never put a password or access token in a command, URL, or shared clipboard. MFA-required native access fails closed until a supported MFA handoff is available.
ssh.scope: SSH grants shell/exec as the device’s configured OS account, not a sandbox. This share does not grant SFTP, SSH forwarding, LAN access, or organization membership. The CLI rechecks authorization when it connects; revocation or expiry refuses new access and terminates share-bound sessions.

shares.revokeBody: New access will be refused. Share-bound remote sessions are terminated by live server checks.
shares.sshAccountHint: An existing Linux/macOS user on that device. The recipient's SSH sessions run as this account, and only this one.
shares.sshAccountInvalid: Enter the device account for SSH: a Linux/macOS user name (lowercase letters, digits, _ and -).
shares.sshRootRefused: root cannot be shared directly. Create an administrator account for the recipient instead.

acct.none: The device reported no login accounts. Create one below.
acct.unavailable: Could not list the device's accounts ({reason}). You can still type an existing account name.
acct.created: Created {name} on the device and chose it.
acct.newAdmin: Administrator (may become root with sudo, no password)
acct.note: A new account has no password: it is reached only through MeshHarbor. The device creates nothing unless its own SSH is enabled, and no administrator if it forbids root sessions.

topo.title: Server topology
topo.intro: Two servers connect directly exactly when an enabled edge joins them, whatever their business zones; without one they do not see each other, even in one zone. Click a server, then another, to add an edge; click an edge to switch it off or remove it. Clients are not drawn: they keep the zone rule. Edges are enforced under
topo.noServers: No device has the central role Server yet. Approve one under Business authority first.
topo.svgTitle: Server topology: servers by country and the edges between them
topo.noEdges: No edges: every server is on its own.

inv.intro: Reported configuration: what each node read from its own kernel (host network namespace only). It is not evidence that a path works and grants no access; the overlay ACL decides that. Freshness is the server's clock.
inv.empty: No node has reported an inventory yet.

dns.saved: Saved. Overlay nodes pick up the change on their next join.
dns.intro1: Give the mesh a DNS suffix so nodes are reachable by name
dns.intro2: instead of overlay IP. Each node runs a local split-DNS resolver: overlay names resolve to overlay IPs, everything else forwards to the upstream nameservers below. Leave the domain blank to disable MagicDNS.
dns.domainHint: Blank disables MagicDNS for the tenant.
dns.upstreamHint: Comma-separated. Blank uses each node's existing system resolvers.

fwd.intro: A managed forward listens on one address of an ingress node, admits only its source CIDRs and relays to a destination. Every change is checked first: port collisions, overlaps, loops, the regional gate and, for the nft backend, the ingress's forwarding settings, which MeshHarbor reports and never changes.

f.name: Name
f.sources: Allowed sources (CIDRs, space or comma separated)
f.public: Public listener (needed for a wildcard address; sources must still be narrower than /0)

fwd.planRefused: Plan refused; nothing was stored or sent to a node.
fwd.planFailed: The plan could not be made.
fwd.changed: This forward changed since it was loaded; the list was reloaded. Check it again.
fwd.confirmRemove: Remove the forward "{name}"? The ingress node stops it at once.

routes.intro1: A node advertises subnet CIDRs it can route (set
routes.intro2: in its agent config). Approve a route to distribute it to every other node in the mesh — they'll route that LAN through this node. Nothing is routed until you approve it.
routes.empty: No node is advertising subnet routes or offering to be an exit node yet.
routes.noLongerOffered: approved, but the device no longer offers it, so no client uses it

acl.title: Overlay ACL
acl.subtitle: Peer visibility + routes — enforced on direct, TURN-relayed and DERP-relayed paths alike
acl.narrowed1: {n} rule(s) narrow ports or protocol. Each node enforces those on the traffic it receives only under
acl.narrowed4: . Either way a port-narrowed rule makes the whole peer visible.
acl.empty1: No overlay rules yet. While enforcement is
acl.empty2: every node sees every peer and all of its approved routes — the pre-ACL behaviour. Add rules, switch to
acl.empty3: to see what they would deny against real traffic, then
acl.sourcesHint: Which nodes this rule grants access FROM.
acl.viaHint: The peer they may reach — and the gateway for its subnet routes.
acl.destHint: CIDRs only — the overlay is L3, so hostnames can never match.
acl.deleteBody: will be removed. If this was the only rule granting a peer, nodes relying on it lose that peer on the next netmap push.

mode.warn: Warn — log what would be denied

hint.off: Rules are stored but ignored — every node sees every peer, as before.
hint.warn: Rules are evaluated and denials are logged, but the permissive netmap still ships. Use this to validate rules against real traffic.
hint.enforce: Rules are applied. A node that no rule grants loses the peer, and an installed peer is explicitly torn down.

v.name: Name is required.
v.sources: At least one source is required.
v.via: At least one via node is required.
v.destinations: At least one destination is required.
v.sourceSel: Every non-catch-all source needs a selection.
v.viaSel: Every node target needs a selection.
v.notCidr: "{cidr}" is not a CIDR — a single address needs a prefix, e.g. 10.0.0.5/32.

tp.title: Tunnel ACL
tp.empty: No tunnel policies defined yet. Server-side ACL is default-deny — until you add at least one policy, every {cmd} request will be rejected with {code}.
tp.subjectsHint: Who this policy applies to. First-match-wins across all policies.
tp.catchAllUsers: (catch-all — matches every user in the tenant)
tp.targetsHint: Which agents this policy lets the subjects reach.
tp.catchAllAgents: (catch-all — matches every agent in the tenant)
tp.allowlistHint: Host + port-range patterns the subjects may reach via the targets.
tp.deleteBody: This will soft-delete {name}. Live tunnel sessions keep working; new {req}s relying on this policy alone will start being rejected with {code}.

err.name: Name is required.
err.subjects: At least one subject is required.
err.targets: At least one target is required.
err.allowlist: At least one allowlist rule is required.
err.subjectId: Each non-AllUsers subject needs an ID.
err.targetId: Agent-ID targets need an Agent ID.
err.host: Each allowlist rule needs a host value.

ek.title: Ephemeral enrollment keys
ek.intro: A reusable credential that enrolls {selfRemoving} devices — CI runners, containers, autoscaled workers. Devices it mints are reaped after inactivity (or immediately on a clean stop), and a restart is a {new} device. Revoking a key stops new enrollments on the next use; devices it already minted die by their own deadline.
ek.labelHint: Display only — name the fleet this key serves
ek.expiresHint: Up to 90 days; the key is dead after this whatever its uses
ek.ttlHint: 60s–7d; blank = server default (15 min). How long a silent device lives before the reaper removes it
ek.copyNow: Copy it now — the key is {notStored} and cannot be shown again. Losing it means minting a new key.

dev.ephemeralTitle: Ephemeral device — removes itself after inactivity or on clean shutdown; removal is final
dev.skewTitleLong: The desktop companion is on v{desktop} while the daemon is on v{daemon} — the companion updates separately (its own .deb on Linux, the .pkg on macOS, a daemon-side swap on Windows)
dev.skewTitle: The desktop companion is on v{desktop} while the daemon is on v{daemon} — the companion updates separately
dev.noDnsDomain: Tenant has no MagicDNS domain configured — bare overlay label
dev.noneHint: Use "Enroll" for a one-line installer per platform — the machine appears here as soon as it enrolls.
dev.hideName: Hide device name when a display name is set

presence.onlineTitle: Online — a control socket is registered
presence.staleTitle: Stale — heartbeat fresh but no socket registered (a half-open network leg or a recent server roll). It should heal within minutes; otherwise restart the MeshHarbor service on the machine.

evict.titleRejoin: Force a new overlay address for “{name}”?
evict.leaves: It leaves the mesh immediately — every peer drops its routes, and traffic to {ip} stops.
evict.released: That address is released back to this organization's pool and may later be assigned to a {different} machine.
evict.rejoins: {name} is still enrolled, so it rejoins automatically on its next connect — with a {different} overlay address. This does not revoke access; to remove the device for good, delete the agent or tunnel client.
evict.gone: Its backing device is no longer enrolled, so it will not come back.
evict.pinned: Anything pinned to the old address stops working — firewall rules, scripts, and any client configured with {cfg}.

tunnelDelete.title: Delete tunnel client?
tunnelDelete.body: Its access token is revoked and, if it joined the overlay, its node is evicted and the overlay address released. The CLI stays installed on the machine and can be re-enrolled with a new token.

rotate.title: Rotate the overlay key of {name}?
rotate.body: The device mints a fresh WireGuard key {onDevice}, saves it and re-joins the mesh under it. Every peer picks the new key up within seconds and the old key stops working everywhere. The server never sees a private key.
rotate.disruptive: Immediate and disruptive by design: every session this device carries in this organization (remote control, SSH over the overlay, tunnels) ends and reconnects.
rotate.offline: The device is offline — the order is queued and runs on its next connect.
rotate.ordered: Key rotation ordered on {name} — it mints a new key, re-joins the mesh and reports back within seconds.
rotate.queuedOffline: {name} is offline — the key rotation is queued and runs on its next connect.

kr.queuedTip: Ordered while the device was offline; it rotates on its next connect.
kr.deliveredTip: The order reached the device; waiting for its answer.
kr.rotatingTip: The device minted its new key and is re-joining the mesh.
kr.rotatedTip: Rotated {at} and joined the mesh under the new key.
kr.notJoinedTip: The device reported a rotation but has not joined the mesh under the new key — read its log.
kr.refusedTip: The device refused the rotation order.
kr.failedTip: The device could not mint or save a new key; its identity is unchanged.
kr.old: agent too old for key rotation
kr.oldTip: This device's agent predates key rotation (0.4.25+). Update it — the order stays queued.

upd.title: Update all agents?
upd.body: Pushes an immediate self-update to every agent in this organization ({total} total, {online} online). Each agent downloads the latest release, installs it, and restarts — active remote-control sessions on updating agents will drop for a few seconds. Offline agents update on their next periodic check.
upd.wont: {n} will not take it from here:
upd.pushed: Update pushed to {name} — it will download, install, and restart shortly.
upd.offline: {name} is offline — it will update on its next periodic check instead.
upd.pushedAll: Update pushed to {delivered} of {requested} agents — offline agents update on their next periodic check.

del.title: Remove this device from the organization?
del.evicted: It is evicted from the overlay mesh immediately — peers drop its routes, and any live remote-control or tunnel session to it ends.
del.stays: The agent stays installed on the host. It can be enrolled again with a new enrollment token, but it comes back with a {fresh}.
del.fresh: new overlay address and a new name
del.pinned: Anything pinned to the old identity stops working — scripts using this agent id, tunnel forwards targeting it, firewall rules on its old overlay address, and any client configured with {cfg}.

join.title: Add to another organization
join.body: {name} keeps its current enrollment and gains a second one. The device connects to both organizations at once; each sees only its own sessions, and the new org gets its own encryption key.
join.old: This device runs an agent version that predates remote org-join. Update it first, or enroll it at the keyboard.
join.offline: This device is offline. It has to be connected to receive the invitation.
join.none: You don't manage devices in any other organization. Ask an admin there to grant you device management, then try again.
join.meshTun: Join the mesh (needs multi-org TUN enabled)
join.restart: This device's agent started with a single organization, so it holds its network adapter exclusively. The join is applied right away, but mesh access begins after the agent restarts — the next auto-update does that.

owner.title: Reassign device owner
owner.body: Owner of {name}. The owner self-controls without an allowlist entry, and consent (email / push) routes to them.

routes.title: Tunnel mesh routes
routes.body: CIDRs that {name} advertises for the mesh ({cmd}). A LAN target IP matching one of these routes is dialed by this agent, so the mesh can reach non-agent devices behind it (a NAS, a printer, a database host). Access is still gated by your {acl} — a route steers the dial, it doesn't authorize it.
routes.none: No routes yet — this agent only reaches its own host.
routes.advertised: Advertised by the agent — click to approve into the routes above:

rc.restartTip: Config saved on the device but not yet in effect.
rc.notPrimary: This org is a secondary on that host; only its primary enrollment may change machine-wide config.
rc.notOptedIn: The device has not opted in to remote configuration.
rc.failedTip: The device could not write its config.
rc.pendingTip: Waiting for the device to reconnect and reconcile.
rc.oldPush: This agent predates remote configuration; nothing is sent to it.
rc.oldReport: This agent applies pushed config but cannot report what it did.

devEdit.title: Edit device
devEdit.name: Device name
devEdit.displayNameHint: Friendly label shown in lists — never propagates anywhere. Leave empty to show the device name.
devEdit.tagsHint: Free-form labels for filtering and search (max 16, 40 chars each). Press Enter to add.
devEdit.nameHintAgent: Propagates to the overlay + MagicDNS label. Peers selecting this device as an exit node BY NAME must update their config — pin by node-id hex to be rename-proof.
devEdit.nameHintClient: Propagates to the overlay + MagicDNS label (server-side rename — the CLI keeps its local machine name).
devEdit.nameEmpty: Device name must not be empty.
devEdit.dnsRenamed: MagicDNS label is now "{name}" — peers resolve it immediately; the device itself picks up its new self-name on its next reconnect.
devEdit.dnsKept: The fleet name changed, but the overlay DNS label could not be updated (kept its old value).

idle.hint: End a remote-desktop session to this device after this long with no input and no change on its screen. The shorter of this and the organization’s limit applies, so it can only tighten the org’s. The device keeps it: an agent that predates it does not. Applies to the next session.

lock.auto: Lock: if locked or idle at the start
lock.hint: Lock this device’s screen when the last remote-desktop session to it ends. “If locked or idle at the start” locks it again only if it was locked, or nobody was at it, when the session began. The device takes the stricter of this and its owner’s own setting, so this can only tighten it. Honoured by service installs on Windows and Linux, where a session can unlock the screen again; a per-user install, or an agent that predates it, does not take it. Applies to the next session.

rcOverlay.hint: Off (default): remote desktop never rides the WireGuard mesh; it connects over the LAN, a direct path or a TURN relay. On: it may take the mesh when that is the best path, and inherits the mesh’s outages. Applies to the next session.

owner.applies: Ask me too (you own this device; "{mode}" applies to you)
owner.skipped: Ask me too (you own this device, so consent is skipped for you)

aria.owner: Apply the consent mode to me, the owner of {name}
aria.lock: Lock {name} when its remote sessions end
aria.rcOverlay: Let remote desktop to {name} use the mesh (overlay)

ext.title: External access — {name}
ext.warn: This lets someone who is {notMember} control this device. They will need its connect code and the password set {onMachine} — and whoever is at the device is still asked before a session starts.
ext.notMember: not a member of your organization
ext.allow: Allow people outside this organization to control this device
ext.allowHint: Off by default. Approving is the second of five gates — on its own it opens nothing.
ext.ceiling: An outside session may at most
ext.ceilingHint: A ceiling, not a grant — the device can be more restrictive, never less. {viewOnly} is the safe answer for anyone you are letting watch rather than work.
ext.expiresHint: Leave empty and the approval stands until someone clears it. Most reasons for granting this — a contractor, a support engagement — have an end date, and an approval nobody has to remember to revoke is one that outlives its reason.
ext.codeHint: This is what an outside person types to reach this device. Rotating it is how you take a leaked code out of circulation — the old one stops working immediately.
ext.orgOff: External access is switched off for the whole organization, so this device will still refuse. An org owner enables it in Settings. It is a separate switch from remote execution and SSH.
ext.tooOld: This device's agent is too old for external access — it cannot tell the person at the machine that the controller is from outside your organization. Update the agent first.
ext.devicePassword: The device itself must also allow it, and must hold the password: {cmd} on the host. That belongs to whoever holds the machine and cannot be set from here — which is the point: the password never reaches this server.

ceil.view: View only — no keyboard or mouse
ceil.files: View, control, clipboard and file transfer

ext.rotateFailed: Could not create a connect code.

logs.title: Agent logs — {name}
logs.noneHint: The agent uploads logs in batches; if it just started or has been idle, give it a minute and hit refresh.
logs.noMatch: No lines match the current filter.

exec.title: Execution policy — {name}
exec.warn: Allowing remote execution on this device lets permitted users run commands as {root} (Linux) or, on Windows, as {system} once the device is anchored (otherwise as the {signedIn} on an attended install, and as SYSTEM in SystemContext mode). It is a separate power from remote control, which is consent-gated and visible on screen.
exec.anchored: Anchored {when}: commands run as {system} through this device's service.
exec.notAnchored: Not anchored: commands run as the {signedIn} (an attended install) or as SYSTEM (SystemContext mode). To run them as SYSTEM, on the device, from an elevated prompt:
exec.accept: Accept remote commands on this device
exec.originate: Allow this device to run commands on OTHER devices (roomler exec)
exec.originateHint: Off by default. Without it, a compromised copy of this device could use its owner's permissions across the whole fleet.
exec.runAsWin: {system} is the default. {signedIn} runs each command as whoever is signed in at the console, and is refused when nobody is. Both go through the device's service, so the device must be anchored.
exec.runAsUnix: {root} is the default. {person} runs each command as whoever is signed in at its own screen, and is refused when nobody is.
exec.runAsPerson: The person at the device's screen
exec.runAsTooOld: This device's agent cannot do that yet: update it, or choose root.
exec.consentHint: {prompt} asks whoever is at the device and denies after 30 s of silence — right for workstations. {unattended} runs immediately — right for servers with nobody sitting at them.
exec.users: Restrict to these users (empty = anyone with the permission)
exec.shells: Allowed shells (empty = any the host supports)
exec.orgOff: Remote execution is switched off for the whole organization, so this device will still refuse. An org owner enables it in Settings.
exec.deviceSwitch: The device itself must also allow it: {cmd} on the host, then restart the service. That switch belongs to whoever holds the machine and cannot be set from here.
exec.anchorSwitch: An anchored device's service checks its own switch as well ({cmd}, elevated).

opt.person: The person at the device's screen

sshp.title: SSH policy — {name}
sshp.warn: Allowing SSH lets permitted users open an {shell} on this device. It is a separate power from remote execution — a session lasts, and it is not one bounded command you can read back afterwards.
sshp.accept: Accept SSH sessions on this device
sshp.originate: Allow this device to open sessions on OTHER devices
sshp.coerced: This device had been set to {signedIn}, which its agent cannot do — it refuses it, so every session was failing at connect time. Update the agent, or pick an account and save to fix it.
sshp.idService: This device serves SSH through its {service}. {signedIn} is whoever is at its console, and a session is refused while nobody is; it is the least surprising choice on a workstation. {daemon} is {system}: choosing it grants full control of this device.
sshp.idAgent: {daemon} is the agent's own: {system} on a service install, but {signedInLower} on an attended one. {signedIn} works on a service install; an attended install serves it only through the device's SYSTEM service, which an administrator turns on there with {cmd}.
sshp.idUnixNamed: {named} is the least surprising choice on a server.
sshp.idUnixPerson: {person} is whoever is signed in at its own screen, and a session is refused while nobody is.
sshp.idUnixDaemon: {daemon} means {root} — choosing it grants root on this device.
sshp.personNeedsNewer: "The person at the device's screen" needs a newer agent on this device.
sshp.unixOnly: Unix only — a Windows device refuses this mode rather than quietly falling back to another account.
sshp.consentHint: {prompt} asks whoever is at the device and denies after 30 s of silence — right for workstations. {unattended} opens immediately — right for servers with nobody sitting at them. A denied prompt burns the grant, so the caller must request a new one rather than re-dialling.
sshp.orgOff: SSH is switched off for the whole organization, so this device will still refuse. An org owner enables it in Settings. It is a separate switch from remote execution.

opt.signedIn: The signed-in user at the device

rcfg.title: Device configuration — {name}
rcfg.intro: This records what you want the device to run. The device applies it the next time it connects — and it may refuse: these switches belong to whoever holds the machine, and a device only accepts them after someone enables {key} on it directly.
rcfg.waitingRestart: Saved on the device, waiting for a restart:
rcfg.execHint: Commands run as the daemon: {root} under systemd; on Windows the {signedIn} (an attended install) or {system} (SystemContext mode). Takes effect immediately on the device; no restart.
rcfg.needExec: You need the {perm} permission to change this. Opening a door you cannot walk through is the same escalation as granting yourself the key.
rcfg.keys: Authorized keys — one OpenSSH public key per line
rcfg.keysHint: Leave the box untouched to keep whatever the device already has. An empty list means {nobody}.
rcfg.accountHint: Cleared = not managed. Unset {onDevice} means a key-list session authenticates and then runs {nothing} — deliberately, so an unread setting cannot quietly hand out SYSTEM/root.
rcfg.port: SSH port (blank = not managed; the device's default is 2222)
rcfg.portHint: 2222 rather than 22 so an existing {sshd} keeps serving the overlay address.
rcfg.needSsh: You need the {perm} permission to change any of these. Handing out authorized keys or an account mode is granting SSH just as much as flipping the switch is.
rcfg.cellsHint: Comma-separated {form} cells the device must not open or advertise — the cell matrix's kill switch. Blank = not managed (the device keeps its own list, built-in {builtin}); {none} = deny nothing. It only ever removes cells, so no extra permission bit; takes effect at the next daemon restart.
rcfg.fpsHint: Comma-separated {form} rates above 60 the device must not grant, {star} for every encoder. Blank = not managed (the device keeps its own, which denies nothing unless set there); {none} = deny nothing. It only ever removes rates, so no extra permission bit; takes effect at the next daemon restart.
rcfg.sshOrgOff: SSH is switched off for the whole organization — a separate switch from remote execution. An org owner enables it in Settings.

st.appliedDetail: The device confirmed this configuration and it is in force.
st.restart: Saved on the device — restart required
st.restartDetail: These keys are written to disk but not yet in effect. The SSH server is spliced into the packet path when the daemon starts, so it will not serve sessions until then.
st.secondary: Refused — this organization is a secondary on that host
st.notOptedIn: Refused — the device has not opted in
st.secondaryDetail: These keys are machine-wide, so only the device’s primary enrollment may change them. Ask an admin of that organization, or configure the host directly.
st.notOptedInDetail: Someone with access to the machine must run {cmd} on it. That switch cannot be set from here — which is the point: it is what keeps a compromised server from opening your devices.
st.failedDetail: It could not write its configuration. Usually a permissions or disk problem on the host.
st.pendingDetail: Requested. The device reconciles when it next connects — an offline device picks this up on its own, nothing needs re-sending.
st.noReportDetail: Agent {v} understands a pushed configuration but not how to say what it did with it. It may well have applied this — there is no way to tell from here. Update the device to find out.
st.tooOldDetail: Agent {v} predates remote configuration, so nothing is sent to it at all. Update it, or set these keys on the host directly.

warn.emptyKeys: SSH is on with an empty key list, which means nobody can connect. Add a key, or leave the key list unmanaged to keep the device’s own.
warn.sshAlone: Turning SSH on grants nothing by itself: the device also needs authorized keys and an account mode. If it already has them, ignore this.
warn.noAccount: You are sending keys but not an account mode. A key-list session on a device whose account mode is unset authenticates and then runs nothing.

stall.tooltip: v{version} is {behind} behind: {first} came out {ago} ago and this device, online, has not installed it.
stall.remedyLinux: A per-user Linux install made before 0.4.138 cannot install updates by itself. Install the current release on it once (sudo apt install ./roomlerd.deb, the Software app, or a re-run of the install script), and it updates itself from then on. On a system install that stopped, check auto_update in 'roomler config ls' and the log ('roomler logs --grep update') on it.
stall.remedyOther: Check auto_update in 'roomler config ls' and the log ('roomler logs --grep update') on it.

cred.soonTip: Its agent token expires on {on}. A device on agent 0.4.135 or later renews it itself 180 days early, so one this close is not renewing: update its agent, or check whether it was removed and re-enrolled elsewhere.
cred.renewableTip: Its agent token expired on {on}. The server still renews it for {days} more day(s) once the device runs agent 0.4.135 or later; after that, re-enroll it.
cred.lostTip: Its agent token expired on {on}, more than {grace} days ago: re-enroll the device.

refusal.auto_update_off: auto-update is off on the device

perm.noScreenTip: The OS has not granted this device screen-capture permission, so the remote screen will be blank. On macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording.
perm.noInputTip: The OS has not granted this device input-injection permission, so remote keyboard and mouse will do nothing. On macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.

search.intro: Type to search across messages, rooms, and people

layout.inCallMuted: In a call, muted — call controls
layout.slugTaken: That slug is already taken — pick another

notFound.body: The page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved.

rooms.noOpen: No open rooms available. Try creating one!
rooms.emptyBody: Create your first room to start chatting, sharing files, or hosting calls with your team.
rooms.deleteBody: This will permanently delete the room and all its messages, files, and members. This cannot be undone.

exec.title: Remote command execution
exec.warn: When enabled, users holding the {perm} permission can run commands on devices that individually opt in. Commands run as {root} (Linux) or, on Windows, as {system} through the device's service once an administrator has anchored it. A Windows device that is not anchored runs them as the {user} on an attended install, and as SYSTEM in SystemContext mode. They are all recorded in the audit log.
exec.allow: Allow remote command execution in this organization
exec.requireSystemHint: A Windows device runs commands as SYSTEM once an administrator has anchored it ({cmd}, elevated). With this on, a device that is not anchored refuses commands instead of running them as whoever is signed in.

settings.offDeviceGate: Off by default. Turning it on does not enable any device on its own — each device must also be allowed individually, and the device's own {setting} setting must permit it.

ssh.title: Roomler SSH
ssh.warn: When enabled, users holding the {perm} permission can open an interactive shell on devices that individually opt in. A session lasts, unlike a single command — and which account it runs as is set per device.
ssh.allow: Allow SSH sessions in this organization

ext.title: External access
ext.warn: When enabled, people {outside} can control devices that individually opt in — the way a support technician reaches a machine they do not administer. They need the device's connect code and a password held {onDevice}, which this server never sees.
ext.allow: Allow people outside this organization to control devices
ext.hint: Off by default, and turning it on opens nothing by itself. Each device must be approved individually, its owner must enable it on the machine and set a password there, and whoever is at the device is still asked before a session starts.

kb.title: Keep busy
kb.body: A controller with input can leave a device's pointer moving in a pattern so it stays active: no screensaver, idle lock or "Away". It pauses whenever someone uses the device. Some organizations do not allow this because it defeats a screen-lock policy.
kb.allow: Allow keep busy in this organization
kb.hint: On by default. Turning it off stops keep busy on every device in the organization, immediately for devices that are online and at the next connect for the rest. A device's owner can also turn it off on that device ({setting}).

rc.title: Remote session features
rc.body: Choose what a remote-desktop session in this organization may use. {ask} allows a feature only when the person at the device approves the session on a prompt that names it; a session nobody there is asked about (an unattended device, your own device, an administrator's forced session) goes without it.
rc.hint: On by default. A device's owner can also turn each one off on that device ({a}, {b}, {c}). A change applies to sessions that start after it.
rc.ask: Ask the person at the device

keys.title: Ephemeral enrollment keys
keys.warn: When enabled, fleet admins can mint {reusable} enrollment keys that create {selfRemoving} devices (CI runners, containers). A key is a standing credential: anyone holding it can enroll devices into this organization until it is revoked, exhausted, or expired.
keys.allow: Allow ephemeral enrollment keys in this organization
keys.hint: Off by default. Turning it OFF is an org-wide revocation: every outstanding key stops working on its next use. Devices already minted are untouched — they remove themselves by their own deadline.

lim.title: Remote session limits
lim.maxHint: A session ends this long after it started, and the person controlling it is told why. No limit by default. A change applies to sessions that start after it.
lim.idle: End a session after no activity for
lim.idleHint: No input from the person controlling it and no change on the screen for this long. They are warned shortly before the end. The device keeps this limit, so a device whose agent predates it does not. No limit by default.

valid.slug: Only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens

roles.title: Roles & Permissions
roles.intro: Roles bundle permissions; members can hold several. Mutations need the {perm} permission — the server rejects anything else. Assign roles to people in the Members section.
roles.empty: No roles yet — create one to start delegating permissions.
roles.name: Name
roles.adminWarn: Administrator bypasses every other permission check — holders can do everything, including managing roles and remote-controlling devices.
roles.deleteBody: Delete {name}? Members holding it lose its permissions immediately.

members.title: Members
members.intro: Assign roles to grant permissions — device access (remote control, device management, audit) is role-driven. Changing roles needs the {perm} permission. New people join via Invites, or add an existing account by email.
members.ownerFixed: The organization owner cannot be removed
members.addBody: Adds an account that already exists on this server. For someone without an account, use Invites instead.
members.noRoles: No roles exist yet — create one in the Roles section first.
members.leaveMsg: Leave this organization? You lose access until someone re-adds or re-invites you.
members.removeMsg: Remove {who} from the organization? Their account is untouched — they just lose access here.

ADMINISTRATOR.label: Administrator
ADMINISTRATOR.description: Bypasses ALL permission checks — grants everything below implicitly.

MANAGE_AGENTS.label: Manage devices
MANAGE_AGENTS.description: Enroll, rename, delete, reassign and set policy for remote-control devices.

REMOTE_CONTROL.label: Remote control
REMOTE_CONTROL.description: Start remote-control sessions against devices the user does NOT own (controlling one's own device never needs this).

VIEW_REMOTE_AUDIT.label: View remote audit log
VIEW_REMOTE_AUDIT.description: Read the remote-control session audit trail.

EXEC_DEVICE.label: Run commands on devices
EXEC_DEVICE.description: Run a command on a device via Fleet RPC. Commands execute as root (Linux) or, on Windows, as the daemon's worker: the signed-in user on an attended install, SYSTEM in SystemContext mode. Also requires the org switch, the device policy, and the device-local key.

VIEW_EXEC_AUDIT.label: View command audit log
VIEW_EXEC_AUDIT.description: Read the Fleet-RPC audit trail — who ran what, where.

SSH_DEVICE.label: SSH to devices
SSH_DEVICE.description: Open an interactive roomler SSH session to a device. Strictly more than a single command: it lasts, and it carries file transfer.

VIEW_SSH_AUDIT.label: View SSH audit log
VIEW_SSH_AUDIT.description: Read the roomler-SSH audit trail — who was granted, or refused, a session.

RECORD_REMOTE_SCREEN.label: Record remote screens
RECORD_REMOTE_SCREEN.description: Record a device’s screen during a remote-control session. The device must allow it, and the person there sees it. A recording outlives the session, so no role gets this by default.

HIVE_RUN.label: Run agent sessions
HIVE_RUN.description: Start and drive AI agent sessions on a device. A session runs as the account the device maps you to — never SYSTEM or root — and only where the device allows it. It runs commands on that device, so no role gets this by default.

audit.ranAsSystemTitle: Ran as SYSTEM through the device's service
audit.ranAsUserTitle: Ran through the device's service as the signed-in user

exec.title: Command audit
exec.subtitle: Every remote command attempted on this organization's devices — including the ones that were refused. Retained for 90 days.
exec.empty: No commands have been attempted yet.

ssh.title: SSH audit
ssh.subtitle: Every SSH session requested on this organization's devices — including the ones that were refused. Retained for 90 days.
ssh.info: These are access {decisions}, not session recordings. Roomler SSH runs peer-to-peer over the mesh, so the server sees who was allowed in and as which account — never what was typed.
ssh.empty: No SSH sessions have been requested yet.

act.title: SSH activity
act.subtitle: What devices reported doing inside their SSH sessions. Retained for 90 days.
act.warn: {emptyNote} Reporting is a per-device setting ({setting}) and is off by default, so a device that never opted in looks exactly like an idle one. These rows are also the device's own account of itself — a compromised host can simply stop talking. The {auditLog} log records every access decision the server made, regardless of what the device says afterwards.
act.emptyNote: An empty list does not mean nothing happened.
act.info: Commands are recorded; {notContent}. There is no terminal recording and no command output here — capturing a session would mean sending whatever was typed, passwords included, off the device. Commands are redacted and truncated before they leave the host.
act.empty: No device has reported SSH activity.

sshAs.systemTitle: Served by the device's SYSTEM service, as SYSTEM
sshAs.consoleTitle: Served by the device's SYSTEM service, as the user signed in at its console
sshAs.agentTitle: The account the agent runs as: root on Linux and macOS, SYSTEM on a Windows service install, and the signed-in user on an attended Windows install.
sshAs.userTitle: The user signed in at the device's console
sshAs.namedTitle: A local account the policy names

console.title: Device console — {name}
console.warn: Commands run with the Roomler daemon's privileges: {root} on Linux. On Windows they run as the {user} on an attended install, or as {system} in SystemContext mode. Every attempt is recorded in the org's execution audit log.
console.empty: No commands run in this session yet.
console.orgOff: Remote execution is switched off for this organization. An org owner can enable it in Settings.
console.deviceOff: This device does not accept remote commands. Enable it in the device’s execution policy.
console.offline: This device is offline — commands will fail until it reconnects.
console.tooOld: This device runs agent {version}, which predates remote execution. Update it first.

enroll.tokenNote: The token below is {single} and expires in {n} minutes. Pick your platform — the recommended command installs everything and enrolls in one step.
enroll.hintSystem: Starts before logon and survives logouts — recommended for servers and unattended machines.
enroll.hintMachine: Machine-wide service that runs while a user is logged in.
enroll.hintUser: Installs and autostarts for your account only — no admin rights needed.
enroll.anchorLabel: Also let administrators run commands as SYSTEM on this device
enroll.anchorHint: The token can then also anchor the device it enrolls, once. Roomler Setup does that itself after a second administrator prompt; after the script or a manual install, run the anchor command below. Give this token only to the person installing it as an administrator.
enroll.thenPaste: then paste the token into the wizard

enrollCmd.anchor: Then anchor it, from the same Administrator PowerShell (replace {placeholder} with the id on the device's page)
enrollCmd.noteWindows: Machine-wide install — run the commands below from an Administrator PowerShell (Terminal (Admin)).
enrollCmd.noteLinux: Installs a root systemd system service (sudo will prompt). Screen capture needs a logged-in session — pick 'This user only' for desktops.
enrollCmd.noteMac: Installs the per-user half (screen sharing + input). To also join the overlay mesh, mint a second enrollment token and append --daemon-token {token} — that adds a root LaunchDaemon and a second device row for this Mac.

consent.denied: Denied — the session will not start.

nl.thanks: Thanks — check your inbox for a confirmation link.
